english: Let $a$ and $b$ be real numbers and let $R$ be the relation on $\mathbb{R}$ given by $R=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}:(x^{2}+ax+b)\,y=4x-3\}$. Suppose that the domain of $R$ is $\mathbb{R}\setminus\{-1\}$ and that $R$ is not a function from its domain to $\mathbb{R}$. Then the value of $a+b$ is ______.
hindi: माना $a$ तथा $b$ वास्तविक संख्याएँ हैं तथा $\mathbb{R}$ पर संबंध $R=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}:(x^{2}+ax+b)\,y=4x-3\}$ है। माना कि $R$ का प्रांत $\mathbb{R}\setminus\{-1\}$ है तथा $R$ अपने प्रांत से $\mathbb{R}$ में फलन नहीं है। तब $a+b$ का मान ______ है।
solution: If $q(x_0)=0$: no $y$ when $x_0\neq\frac34$; every $y\in\mathbb{R}$ when $x_0=\frac34$ (the whole vertical line $x=\frac34$ lies in $R$)
Domain $\mathbb{R}\setminus\{-1\}\Rightarrow q(-1)=0$ and any other root of $q$ is $\frac34$, so $q=(x+1)^{2}$ or $q=(x+1)\left(x-\frac34\right)$
$q=(x+1)^{2}$: each $x\neq-1$ has exactly one image, $R$ is a function, rejected
$q=(x+1)\left(x-\frac34\right)=x^{2}+\frac14x-\frac34$: the line $x=\frac34$ meets $R$ in infinitely many points, so $R$ is not a function
solution_full: Write $q(x)=x^{2}+ax+b$. For a fixed real $x_0$, the elements of $R$ with first entry $x_0$ are the solutions $y$ of $q(x_0)\,y=4x_0-3$.
Case $q(x_0)\neq0$: exactly one solution $y=\dfrac{4x_0-3}{q(x_0)}$, so $x_0$ is in the domain with one image.
Case $q(x_0)=0$ and $x_0\neq\frac34$: the equation reads $0=4x_0-3\neq0$, no solution, so $x_0$ is not in the domain.
Case $q(x_0)=0$ and $x_0=\frac34$: the equation reads $0=0$, true for every $y$; the whole vertical line $x=\frac34$ lies in $R$, so $\frac34$ is in the domain with infinitely many images.
So the domain of $R$ is $\mathbb{R}$ minus the roots of $q$ different from $\frac34$, and $R$ fails to be a function exactly when $\frac34$ is a root of $q$.

Domain $=\mathbb{R}\setminus\{-1\}$: $-1$ must be a root of $q$, and the other root (if different) cannot be removed from the domain, so it must be $\frac34$. Hence $q(x)=(x+1)^{2}$ or $q(x)=(x+1)\left(x-\frac34\right)$.
If $q(x)=(x+1)^{2}$, then $\frac34$ is not a root, every $x\neq-1$ has exactly one image and $R$ is the function $y=\dfrac{4x-3}{(x+1)^{2}}$; this contradicts the hypothesis.
Hence $q(x)=(x+1)\left(x-\frac34\right)=x^{2}+\frac14x-\frac34$, where the vertical line $x=\frac34$ meets $R$ in infinitely many points, so $R$ is not a function.
originality_note: New: a relation defined by a linear equation in y whose coefficient vanishes; the domain is read from the roots of the coefficient and the vertical-line test fails only on a degenerate line where the equation becomes 0 = 0 (way 3: two conditions, domain and not-a-function, pin down the quadratic). Closest known: 'find the domain of y = (4x-3)/(x^2+ax+b)' and 'which of these relations is a function'. Different because: the relation is not written as y = ..., and the decisive point x = 3/4 is in the domain with infinitely many images.
blueprint_concepts: Relation: definition, domain, codomain and range
Definition of a function; vertical line test; identical functions

concept_use.Relation: definition, domain, codomain a: The domain of R is read off as R minus the roots of x^2+ax+b other than 3/4, which forces -1 to be a root.
concept_use.Definition of a function; vertical line: The vertical line x = 3/4 lies entirely in R, which separates the case (x+1)(x-3/4) (not a function) from (x+1)^2 (a function).

stem_review: Read as a student: every set, relation and symbol is defined before use, every condition is stated, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed independently in Python by brute-force enumeration, is unique and equals the Answer Plan (negative decimal). Changed: No change.
key_step: Recognising that at x = 3/4 the equation becomes 0 = 0, so that vertical line lies in R.
justification: Two ideas linked: domain from the roots of the coefficient, and a non-obvious failure of the vertical-line test; a numerical answer with a case to reject. Comparable to 2026-P1-Q7 (L3) implications needing a counter-case.
